name: wsb-post-classifier
removed_classes: the catch-all fifth class was removed on purpose; it is not part of this model

provenance.note: Fine-tuned from the published ProsusAI/finbert checkpoint. The original 3-way sentiment head (positive/negative/neutral) is discarded and replaced with a fresh 4-way classification head; the whole BERT encoder is then fine-tuned on the hand-labelled WSB data. Not a TF-IDF/linear model.
provenance.legacy_model: model.joblib (the previous TF-IDF + logistic-regression model) is kept for reference and can still be served with --model model.joblib

architecture.head: linear(768 -> 4) on the [CLS] pooled output, replacing the original 3-label head
architecture.trained_on: NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1660 Ti (6 GB), ~31 min

training_data.split: 80% train (6400) / 20% held-out test (1600), stratified on (year, label), seed 42 - the exact same split as the legacy logreg model, verified via split_test_ids.json
training_data.labelling: every post read by hand against LABEL_RUBRIC.md; no model-generated or keyword-generated labels

metrics.note: this model's own scores: it was trained on the 80% split only, so the 20% is a genuine held-out set for it. Reproducible via smoke_test.py.

finetune_vs_previous_logreg.note: same 80/20 split, same 1600 held-out posts, same labels - directly comparable

why_finetune_finbert.summary: A domain-pretrained transformer beats TF-IDF + logistic regression on every class and on every year, with the largest gains on the two smallest classes.
why_finetune_finbert.domain_pretraining: FinBERT was pretrained on financial text (Reuters TRC2-financial + Financial PhraseBank), so its encoder already encodes market vocabulary before it ever sees WSB.
why_finetune_finbert.context: Unlike bag-of-ngrams, the encoder reads word order and context, which is what separates a directional opinion from a joke and a claim from an analysis.
why_finetune_finbert.overfitting: Fine-tuning regularises better here: the train/test gap drops from 0.248 to 0.165.

known_weaknesses: GENUINE_OPINION is still the weakest class (F1 0.51): a directional opinion with no analysis is genuinely hard to separate from a joke from text alone, though it improved by 0.09 over the previous model
the model overfits: train accuracy 0.895 vs 0.731 held-out
text is truncated to 256 tokens, so the longest DD posts are only partly read by the model (the previous TF-IDF model saw the whole text)
2019-2023 posts in Arctic Shift often have an empty body, so those years are classified from the title alone
accuracy is dominated by NOISE_MEME (58% of data); use macro-F1 or per-class metrics to judge changes
serving needs torch + transformers and ~440 MB of model weights; the previous model was 8.6 MB and stdlib-servable
